surface: /food (replaces the desk Food object's link to beliapp.co)
decision: Which visual language should the drill-down food map use?
invariants: same 73 places (Beli 'Been' list, ranks 1-73, OCR of Savar's 2026-10-13 screen recording)
same drill path: World -> country -> province -> cluster -> place card; Esc goes back one level
same ranked list beside the map, in step with the map
same card fields: rank, score, price, cuisines, area, Google Maps link
same clustering and label rules (shared core.js)
Equal Earth projection, Antarctica removed, world view cropped to 66N-42S
prototype: mockups/food-map/ (gitignored; open index.html as a file)

options.bet: Quiet flat map in the site's tokens
options.benefit: Fastest to read; matches inner pages; easy dark mode
options.cost: Least memorable; not a desk object

options.bet: Folded paper travel map, push pins, receipt card
options.benefit: Continues the desk's physical objects; food-specific card
options.cost: More drawing work; typewriter text scans slower
options.risk: Costume if the texture is overdone

options.bet: Dark halftone dot land, score bubbles
options.benefit: Most striking; scores on every pin; coarse coastlines look intentional
options.cost: Dark block on a white site; canvas redraw per frame
options.risk: Borders hard to read; dashboard mood

options.bet: Tilted 3D board, standing flag pins, camera tilts lower per level (CSS 3D, no three.js)
options.benefit: Depth and a flying-in feel without three.js
options.cost: No free pan or wheel zoom; far edge small
options.risk: Harder to read; more motion; weakest on phones

evidence: Each artifact is one row: world, British Columbia, Around Vancouver with the card open, phone with the card open. Rendered with headless Chrome from file:// (no server); runtime test tools/smoke.cjs passes for all four.
known_gaps: 29 of 73 pins approximate (area centre plus spread); exact locations needed for the build
Natural Earth coastline is coarse at city zoom; build needs OSM coastline per city area
light mode only; phone world view small
